t:
That the second sentence of section 49(a) of the Arms Control and Disarmament Act, as amended (22 U.S.C. 2589(a)), is amended by inserting immediately after “$30,000,000”, the following: “, and for the two fiscal years I960 through 1970, the sum of $18,500,000,”,
 
    (b) 
Section 49(a) of such Act is amended by inserting at the end thereof a new sentence as follows; “Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, not more than $7,000,000 of the funds appropriated pursuant to the preceding sentence for fiscal years 1969 through 1970 may be used for the purpose of research, development, and other studies conducted in whole or in part outside the Agency, whether by other government agencies or by public or private institutions or persons: 
Provided, That this limitation shall not apply to field test, activities conducted pursuant to the authority of this Act.
”

fable.w: This section authorizes appropriations and caps the amount that may be spent on research conducted outside the Agency. The mention of "public or private institutions or persons" is tempting, but it describes who may perform funded research (essentially contracts or grants), not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: may be used for the purpose of research, development, and other studies conducted in whole or in part outside the Agency, whether by other government agencies or by public or private institutions or persons

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the expenditure of federal funds for research and studies conducted by outside entities. It does not require the federal government to consult with, coordinate with, or seek input from these outside entities before making a decision. The relationship described is that of a funder and a contractor/grantee, which falls under the exclusion for applications for grants or contracts. There is no advisory board, public hearing, comment period, or right to sue mentioned.
qwen_block.s: Not more than $7,000,000 of the funds appropriated pursuant to the preceding sentence for fiscal years 1969 through 1970 may be used for the purpose of research, development, and other studies conducted in whole or in part outside the Agency, whether by other government agencies or by public or private institutions or persons

opus.w: This section raises an authorization of appropriations and caps how much of those funds can be spent on research done outside the Agency. Private institutions or people who do research under contract are not being consulted on a federal decision; this is closer to contracting, which the definition excludes. There is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation requirement, rulemaking or right to sue.
opus.s: not more than $7,000,000 of the funds appropriated pursuant to the preceding sentence for fiscal years 1969 through 1970 may be used for the purpose of research, development, and other studies conducted in whole or in part outside the Agency, whether by other government agencies or by public or private institutions or persons
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the text mentions research "conducted in whole or in part outside the Agency" by "public or private institutions or persons." But that only caps how much appropriated money can go to outside research contracts. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision, and contracting for research is not participation.

qwen_chat.w: This provision authorizes the expenditure of funds for research and development conducted by outside entities. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision; it simply allows the government to hire outside entities to perform work. This is a procurement or contracting activity, not a participatory decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Act, not more than $7,000,000 of the funds appropriated pursuant to the preceding sentence for fiscal years 1969 through 1970 may be used for the purpose of research, development, and other studies conducted in whole or in part outside the Agency, whether by other government agencies or by public or private institutions or persons:
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions studies conducted by "public or private institutions or persons."
Resolution: This provision authorizes the expenditure of funds for research and development. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision; it simply allows the government to hire outside entities to perform work. This is a procurement or contracting activity, not a participatory decision-making process.
